live_handoff.state: #56 WAS NOT A TEMPLATE-REPLAY GAP. madc had NO std::initializer_list support at all: a braced list on a class type lowered as a PARENTHESISED ctor-argument list, so vector<int> v{1,2,3} compiled as v(1,2,3) — 1 became the size and 3 was handed to allocator<int> (the undefined MIR import). The COPY form = {1,2,3} threaded only init_list[0], selecting vector(size_type) with n==1, which compiles CLEAN through --emit=c11 and SILENTLY yields a one-element vector. Implemented [dcl.init.list]/3-4: TokenDecl::ctor_args_braced carries the spelling; DataDef::is_std_initializer_list() lives in madc_mangle.cpp (the one sanctioned home — the LANGUAGE names this type, so no generic question can replace it, and g++ does the same test); DataDefCLASS::collect_initializer_list_ctors() is ONE candidate rule read by BOTH phases (the parser must not deduce a member-template ctor from list ELEMENTS — vector<double> d{1.5,2.5} deduced vector(_InputIterator,_InputIterator) and died in tsubst); the literal is (IL){ (E[]){e...}, N } with an explicit decay CAST to E* (without it c2mir checks the braces against the scalar member). CLASS element types decline (vector<string>{"a","b"} needs a CONSTRUCTED backing array; it faulted inside basic_string::_M_construct) so they stay on the pre-existing loud path. ⚠️ THREE DEFECTS THAT SHIPPED IN v0.80.0 came out of this: (a) vector<int> e{} SIGSEGV — `T x{}` is spelled internally as `x = x` and the copy ctor read its own uninitialized storage; fixed at the CONSTRUCTION site, not the parse site, because the v16 freeze both DETECTS and REBUILDS that shape as CIR_GLOBALF_CLASS_VALUE_INIT (a parse-side fix silently dropped the marker — the Phase 6 v16 unit test caught it, and the restore lane needed covering too). (b) declarations before a switch's first case label rejected when they lead with a qualifier/tag keyword (`const char *cs;`) — NOT freeze-only. (c) a struct member typed with a class-qualified nested type (`ios_base::fmtflags _M_mask;`) rejected, which stopped <iomanip> on its FIRST line of content; every other declaration position already folded that chain, so the fix is adoption of parseDeclaration's fold, now Program::fold_class_qualified_nested_type().

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
